title: Conservation of Atoms in Reactions
seo_title: Grade 7 Conservation of Mass Worksheets: Counting Atoms and Balanced Equations
standard_text: Develop and use a model to describe how the total number of atoms does not change in a chemical reaction and thus mass is conserved.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on conservation of atoms and mass (NGSS MS-PS1-5): counting atoms in chemical equations, balanced equations, missing coefficients, and closed vs. open systems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed.
key_sub: The number of each kind of atom is the same before and after a reaction, so mass is conserved.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged to make new substances. No atoms are created or destroyed, so the number of each kind of atom is the same before and after, and the total mass stays the same in a closed system.

Example: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. Left: 4 H and 2 O. Right: 4 H and 2 O. The equation is balanced.

Count atoms with coefficient × subscript. In an open container a gas can escape, so the measured mass may drop, but the atoms still exist.

Example

In CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O, how many O atoms are on the right?

CO₂: 2

2H₂O: 2 × 1 = 2

2 + 2

Answer: 4

Example

25 g + 15 g react in a sealed bag. Mass after?

Closed system.

Answer: 40 g

Common mistakes

  • Thinking mass is lost when a gas forms. The gas still has mass.
  • Changing subscripts to balance an equation. Change only coefficients.
  • Thinking products have more atoms because they are new substances.

faq.q: Why is mass conserved in a chemical reaction?
faq.a: The same atoms are rearranged into new substances. No atoms are created or destroyed.

faq.q: How do you check if an equation is balanced?
faq.a: Count each kind of atom on both sides using coefficient × subscript. Every kind must match.

faq.q: Why does an open cup of vinegar and baking soda lose mass?
faq.a: A gas forms and escapes into the air. In a sealed container the mass would stay the same.

items.q: Kai studies photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2. How many carbon atoms are in the products (right side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 6.
